data.title: Disruption of hippocampal upstream regulators of mTOR and insulin pathways in Down syndrome with Alzheimer's disease neuropathology: Preliminary observations
data.authors: Nordbeck AJ; Martá-Ariza M; Ek Olofsson H; Kanshin E; Ueberheide B et al.

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.model_system: Human post-mortem hippocampus (Down syndrome with AD neuropathology vs neurotypical controls)
data.finding: Spatial transcriptomics plus localized proteomics on human post-mortem hippocampus show that mTOR pathway signalling is significantly altered in specific hippocampal subfields in Down syndrome with Alzheimer's disease neuropathology, while insulin pathway signalling is altered specifically in dentate granule neurons — pointing to subregion- and cell-type-specific mTOR/insulin dysregulation rather than a uniform whole-tissue shift. Explicitly framed by the authors as preliminary.
data.abstract_excerpt: Down syndrome (DS) is caused by a complete or partial trisomy of chromosome 21, resulting in variable intellectual disabilities and a high risk for early-onset Alzheimer's disease (DS-AD). Dysregulation of the mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR) and insulin (INS) signaling pathways has been reported in DS. We hypothesized that upstream alterations in these two pathways contribute to hippocampal dysfunction in DS-AD.
